bull.b: The approximately $1.0 billion liquidity position and runway through 2029 give CG Oncology substantial capacity to fund clinical development and prepare for potential commercialization. Very low debt further reduces financing pressure while the company advances its pipeline.

A Phase 3 registrational trial approaching topline data represents a meaningful maturation of the lead program. Progress through late-stage development can improve regulatory visibility and create a clearer path toward commercial revenue if the results support approval.

Publication of clinical results in The Lancet Oncology and additional trial data strengthen the external evidence base for cretostimogene. A growing body of evidence may support regulatory discussions and the company’s ambition to address a broad bladder-cancer patient population.

bear.b: Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that CG Oncology is not yet self-funding its operations. Continued clinical investment will require substantial liquidity, and ongoing negative cash generation could eventually increase dependence on external financing.

Very small and sharply contracting revenue indicates that the company has limited commercial scale today. Until its investigational therapy reaches broader commercialization, the business remains primarily dependent on development milestones rather than established operating revenue.

Large operating and net losses, combined with rising quarterly expenses, indicate that the current cost base substantially exceeds revenue. This weak earnings profile may persist while late-stage trials and regulatory preparation continue, extending the period before profitability.
